schol.title: NMSU International Student and Scholar Services - Scholarships (International Competitive Scholarship)

test_policy.notes: First-time freshmen qualify with a secondary-school GPA of 2.75 or an ACT composite of 21 or an SAT of 1060 (or GED 480 / HiSET 45), so scores are an alternative to GPA rather than required. International applicants also need a foreign credential evaluation from a NACES-approved agency.

requirements.notes: International undergraduate applications are processed by International Student and Scholar Services; the $50 fee cannot be waived or deferred. Transcripts, test scores and credential evaluations must come directly from the school, testing agency or evaluation agency (email admissions@nmsu.edu). The process can take up to 3 months.

deadlines.label: Fall 2027: application must be initiated
deadlines.notes: Published as 'July 1 (application initiated)' with no year, so fall 2027 is assumed. NMSU says it has no university-wide deadline beyond these dates but advises applying 6 months or more ahead.

deadlines.label: Fall 2027: all supporting documents received
deadlines.notes: Published as 'July 15 (all documents submitted)' with no year, so fall 2027 is assumed.

deadlines.label: International Competitive Scholarship window closes (fall 2027)
deadlines.notes: The application is open May 15 to July 15 for fall (year not printed, so 2027 is assumed) and closes earlier once the available awards are used; it is only open to students with an I-20.

english_policy.waiver_notes: Citizens of the listed English-speaking countries (e.g. UK, Ireland, Canada except Quebec, Australia, New Zealand, Singapore, Philippines, South Africa, Nigeria, Kenya and others) are exempt. Others may be waived after two full years at a U.S. high school or 24 semester credits at a U.S. college with a 2.0 GPA. NMSU may still require any applicant to submit a test. Scores must be less than two years old; institutional TOEFL is not accepted. Admitted international students take NMSU's English Language Placement Test.

english.notes: The admissions page states 'minimum TOEFL of 3.5 iBT', which is the new 1-6 scale. An old-scale (0-120) admission minimum is not printed on that page.

aid.notes: International Competitive Scholarship: a tuition discount (in-state instead of out-of-state tuition) plus a $100 cash stipend each fall and spring, for new degree-seeking F-1 students with an I-20, renewable up to 8 semesters. Freshman eligibility e.g. GPA 3.50 with TOEFL 68 / IELTS 6.0 / Duolingo 95, or GPA 3.25 with TOEFL 79 / IELTS 6.5 / Duolingo 100, or GPA 3.50 for students from English-exempt countries. Awards are limited and competitive and the separate application closes when awards run out. (TOEFL values here are the scholarship tiers, not the admission minimum.)

sat.note: NMSU's pages read do not print a separate SAT code; look it up in the College Board code search.

act.note: No ACT code is printed on the pages read; look it up at act.org.

toefl.note: The FAQ gives institution code 4531 for TOEFL, IELTS, GRE and Duolingo results.

ielts.note: The FAQ says to use institution code 4531 for IELTS results; IELTS has no numeric ETS code.

duolingo.note: The FAQ says to use institution code 4531 for Duolingo results.

pte.note: PTE is not listed among NMSU's accepted undergraduate tests.
